response.text:
Search found relevant temporal-gating precedents, but no verified 2024–2026 paper establishing this exact NextItNet modification. [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) provides the causal dilated residual backbone. [Time-LSTM](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2017/504) introduces interval-conditioned gates to distinguish short- and long-term interests; [TLSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04760) uses a neural time gate to regulate their contributions based on elapsed time. More recently, [IntervalLLM (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.23209) investigates irregular interaction intervals, supporting their relevance without establishing effectiveness for convolutional recommenders.

Practical hypothesis, inferred from these mechanisms: retain one NextItNet and modulate its convolutional residual updates using item features plus clipped, scaled log1p elapsed gaps. Preserve the skip pathway so large gaps need not erase persistent preferences. A multiplier such as 1 + α·tanh(MLP(features, gap)), with α initialized to zero, starts with the baseline update unchanged; this adapts the zero-initialized gating principle of [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887), rather than reproducing its identity-block initialization. Compare against the same network without temporal modulation using macro validation HR@10.

Implementation safeguards: compute adjacent gaps only between valid historical events; optionally use t_i−t_{i−d} for dilation-specific spacing. Mask padding before gap transforms and after convolutional updates, and normalize each position across channels without pooling future positions. Never use the held-out target timestamp or its gap; prediction must use observed history timestamps only. For left-padded histories, read the final nonpadding position. Timestamp alignment must remain available through training, diagnosis and the embedded predictor; item IDs alone cannot reconstruct event-specific spacing.
